events.summary: President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to launch a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

Marcello Dell'Utri, a close ally of former Italian Premier Silvio Berlusconi, was apprehended in Beirut after fleeing Italy as a fugitive.

Silvio Berlusconi selects former Milan and Fiorentina goalkeeper Giovanni Galli as his candidate for mayor of Florence in the June elections.

Silvio Berlusconi was injured after a man threw a model of Milan cathedral at him during a rally in Milan, and he was kept in hospital overnight.

President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to lead a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

Pier Silvio Berlusconi reportedly threatened to close two Mediaset programmes, including Domenica Live, unless they cut or toned down sexual content, following an internal investigation and a parents' movement complaint.

Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi faced political protest for attempting to directly nominate the heads of state television service Rai, reportedly tipping McDonald's Italy head Mario Resca to be its new president.

Fininvest, the company at the apex of Silvio Berlusconi's business empire, announced it was reducing its holding in the Mediaset TV network to just over 34%.
The Italian senate began debating a controversially amended communications bill that critics say would enable Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to extend his influence over the country's media.

Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi pledged to bypass an attempt to curb his media power by having his government impose an emergency decree to protect his television empire from being dismantled.

The Italian cabinet passed an emergency decree to save one of Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's private TV channels, Retequattro, overruling a court decision that it should move to satellite by year-end.
Silvio Berlusconi was placed under investigation by Italian magistrates on suspicion of pressuring Italy's media watchdog to block a state television talk show he considered hostile.

Mediaset, the media empire of Silvio Berlusconi, acquired non-exclusive rights to broadcast home games of Juventus, Inter, and AC Milan on its digital channels for the next three seasons in a €86m deal.

Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi announces that reviewing the legislation guaranteeing parties equal access to TV air time will be a top priority in the new year, with discussion on the working agenda from January 7.

Silvio Berlusconi reportedly arranged with a notary public to register the name and logos of a new Freedom party.

Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's government signals it will accept a parliamentary inquiry into police violence at the G8 summit in Genoa, after cabinet ministers persuaded him that blocking it would be seen as a cover-up.

Anti-corruption prosecutors in Spain are considering whether to reopen a suspended investigation into alleged tax fraud involving Silvio Berlusconi's holdings in Spain's Telecinco TV channel, just two weeks after he lost immunity from prosecution.
Silvio Berlusconi hosts the G8 summit in Genoa, preparing extensively for the event and aiming to improve his international image.

Italy's highest court is expected to rule on David Mills's bribery conviction appeal, a decision that will affect Silvio Berlusconi's pending Milan corruption trial.
Silvio Berlusconi was placed under investigation by Italian magistrates on suspicion of pressuring Italy's media watchdog to block a state television talk show he considered hostile.

Italy's highest appeals court stated that it quashed David Mills's conviction for taking a bribe from Silvio Berlusconi due to a statute of limitations technicality, not because it believed him innocent.
Leonardo leaves his post as Milan manager by mutual consent after his relationship with owner Silvio Berlusconi deteriorated following public criticism of team selection.

A Sicilian appeals court ruled there was no evidence that Marcello Dell'Utri, a long-term ally of Silvio Berlusconi, had links with the Mafia after 1992, effectively clearing Berlusconi of accusations that his entry into politics was sponsored by the Mafia.
Silvio Berlusconi dismissed sex and drug allegations against him as "made-up stories" and hinted the mafia may have framed him in reprisal for recent police successes.
Four ministers loyal to Gianfranco Fini resigned from Silvio Berlusconi's government, bringing the administration closer to a confidence vote in parliament.

Judges in Palermo ruled that Marcello Dell'Utri, who spearheaded Silvio Berlusconi's entry into politics, was also an intermediary between Berlusconi and the Sicilian mafia, and that Berlusconi paid enormous sums to Cosa Nostra for protection and to safeguard his TV network's relay stations on Sicily.
Silvio Berlusconi was flying to Sochi for an unscheduled meeting with Vladimir Putin, shortly after WikiLeaks published US diplomatic cables alleging a secret business association between them.
Silvio Berlusconi wins two confidence votes, avoiding resignation and blunting a rebellion by followers of former deputy Gianfranco Fini, though political uncertainty remains.

Silvio Berlusconi is formally placed under investigation by Milan prosecutors on suspicion of paying for sex with a 17-year-old girl and abusing his position as prime minister to cover up the alleged relationship.

A police trade union criticized the reported use of policewomen's outfits in striptease shows at Silvio Berlusconi's villa, as a parliamentary committee began considering whether to allow part of the investigation to proceed.
Prosecutors investigating Silvio Berlusconi were told he would not answer their questions, as a witness, Nadia Macri, came forward with new evidence against him.

Prosecutors investigating Silvio Berlusconi said they expected to recommend that the Italian prime minister be charged with abusing his position to cover up allegations that he had paid an underage prostitute.
Prosecutors announce they will ask for Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to be put on trial over his relationship with a teenager alleged to have been an underage prostitute.
A Milan judge ruled that Silvio Berlusconi should stand trial on 6 April on charges of paying an underage prostitute and abusing his position as prime minister to cover it up.
Silvio Berlusconi publicly stated he was not worried about standing trial on charges of paying an underage prostitute and abusing his official position.
Silvio Berlusconi underwent a four-hour jaw and dental operation under general anaesthetic to repair damage from a 2009 attack, was discharged from hospital in Milan, and returned to his villa.
The trial of Silvio Berlusconi on charges of paying for sex with a 17-year-old and abuse of office is set to begin in Italy.
Italian MPs vote to challenge the legitimacy of Silvio Berlusconi's underage prostitution trial, setting up a constitutional face-off that could derail the case.
Silvio Berlusconi's trial on charges of paying an underage prostitute and abusing his office formally opened in Milan, with the alleged escort declining to attach herself to the case.
Silvio Berlusconi denied accusations that he paid a teenage runaway for sex, saying he gave €45,000 to Karima el Mahroug to help her launch a beauty business.

Three associates under investigation in a related prostitution case against Silvio Berlusconi fell out, with Nicole Minetti's defense document reportedly blaming Emilio Fede and Lele Mora for introducing the prime minister to Karima El Mahroug, while Fede denied the memorandum and accused Mora.
Milan prosecutors ask for an Anglo-Italian former showgirl and two others to be put on trial for allegedly procuring 33 young women for so-called bunga bunga sex sessions at Silvio Berlusconi's home.

Voters in Milan go to the polls in a mayoral runoff widely seen as a crucial test of Silvio Berlusconi's diminished political standing, after a minister resigned over his remarks about Italy's judges.
Silvio Berlusconi suffered a humiliating political defeat in his home city of Milan when his party's candidate for mayor, Letizia Moratti, was ousted in a runoff by leftwing lawyer Giuliano Pisapia.

A Milan appeals court ordered Silvio Berlusconi's company Fininvest to pay over €560m in compensation to rival Carlo De Benedetti for bribery of a judge in the battle for control of publisher Mondadori, with the judges stating Berlusconi was "jointly responsible" for the corruption.
Two people alleged to have blackmailed Silvio Berlusconi were arrested in Rome.

Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's government released a letter to European Union authorities outlining reforms, including public asset sales and employment law changes, to address Italy's debt crisis.

Silvio Berlusconi's coalition government edged closer to breaking up as he struggled to draw up economic reforms to satisfy EU leaders, with Northern League leader Umberto Bossi expressing pessimism about the government's survival.

Silvio Berlusconi faces a series of court hearings in December on charges including fraud, bribery, and paying an underage girl for sex, after losing the immunity from prosecution he had as prime minister.
Silvio Berlusconi's resignation became a question of when, not if, as his majority in parliament was thrown into doubt by deserting MPs.
Silvio Berlusconi informs Italy's president that he will resign as prime minister after passing EU-demanded economic reforms, though he says it will be sometime in November.
Silvio Berlusconi resigns as Italian prime minister.
Silvio Berlusconi fails in a legal bid to stop David Mills from giving evidence in his corruption trial.
Testimony of David Mills in Silvio Berlusconi's bribery trial was delayed as lawyers and judges debated how he should give evidence via video link to the Milan court.

A bribery trial against former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi over payments to British lawyer David Mills failed to reach a verdict after judges ruled the statute of limitations had expired.
Silvio Berlusconi gave the clearest indication yet that he will seek re-election as Italian prime minister in 2013.
George Clooney is called as a witness in Silvio Berlusconi's trial in Milan, where Berlusconi is accused of paying an underage prostitute for sex.

Milan owner Silvio Berlusconi was found guilty of tax fraud and sentenced to four years in prison, with a three-year ban from public office, in a case involving Mediaset film and television rights; he denied wrongdoing and is expected to appeal.
Silvio Berlusconi says a tax fraud verdict against him is politically motivated.
Silvio Berlusconi confirms he will run again for prime minister of Italy.
Judges in Milan ordered a nationwide hunt for Karima el-Mahroug after she failed to appear in court to testify in Silvio Berlusconi's trial on charges of paying for underage sex.
Berlusconi said he would withdraw from the election race if Mario Monti agreed to stand for office at the head of a coalition that included his Freedom People party.
Senior judges in Milan rebuke Silvio Berlusconi after he blamed his large alimony payments on "feminist, communist" magistrates.

A Milan court rejected Silvio Berlusconi's request to suspend his trial over charges of paying for sex with an underage prostitute and abuse of office, ordering proceedings to continue despite his election campaign.
Milan owner Silvio Berlusconi apologizes for calling Mario Balotelli "a rotten apple" but claims neither he nor vice-president Adriano Galliani have discussed buying the Manchester City striker.

AC Milan, owned by Silvio Berlusconi, agreed a deal for Mario Balotelli to leave Manchester City, with the timing during the January transfer window prompting political rivals to question whether it was intended to win votes ahead of parliamentary elections.
Paolo Berlusconi, brother of former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, used a racial slur to describe Mario Balotelli before the footballer's first match for AC Milan.

Karima "Ruby" el-Mahroug, the woman at the center of Silvio Berlusconi's sex trial, accused prosecutors of psychological warfare and denied having sex with Berlusconi, while admitting she had lied about her origins.

Prosecutors in the Rubygate trial demand that Silvio Berlusconi serve six years in prison and be banned from public office for life for allegedly paying for sex with an underage prostitute and abusing his office to cover it up.
A verdict is expected in Silvio Berlusconi's trial in Milan on charges of paying for sex with an underage girl and abusing his office to cover it up.

Italy's parliament was suspended after the Democratic Party joined Silvio Berlusconi's followers in voting for a stoppage in protest at a supreme court decision to fast-track his final appeal against a tax fraud conviction.
Italy's supreme court is due to decide on Silvio Berlusconi's final appeal against a tax fraud conviction, which if upheld could bar him from public office for five years.
Italy's supreme court upheld Silvio Berlusconi's fraud conviction, his first definitive conviction, triggering a political crisis over whether the senate will expel him.
Italian President Giorgio Napolitano says Silvio Berlusconi's definitive tax fraud conviction must be respected and warns that a government crisis over the issue would be fatal.
Silvio Berlusconi called for fresh Italian elections as soon as possible after pulling his ministers out of Enrico Letta's grand coalition government.

Silvio Berlusconi announced he would instruct his party to vote against a motion of no confidence in Enrico Letta's coalition government, a tacit admission that he had lost the backing of a sizable number of his own politicians and no longer had power of veto over government policy.
Silvio Berlusconi's lawyer says he intends to request that Berlusconi serve his one-year tax fraud sentence through a community service placement.
Italy's upper house of parliament voted to oust Silvio Berlusconi following his conviction for tax fraud.

Pier Silvio Berlusconi reportedly threatened to close two Mediaset programmes, including Domenica Live, unless they cut or toned down sexual content, following an internal investigation and a parents' movement complaint.
Marcello Dell'Utri, a close ally of former Italian Premier Silvio Berlusconi, was apprehended in Beirut after fleeing Italy as a fugitive.
A Milan court rules that former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi will serve his year-long tax fraud sentence through part-time community service at a home for the elderly.
Milan president Silvio Berlusconi said the club would decide on a solution for coach Clarence Seedorf at the next board meeting, describing him as part of the club's past.

A Milan appeals court acquitted former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi of charges of paying for sex with an underage prostitute and abusing his office to cover it up, overturning a prior conviction.

Italy begins the process of electing a new president, a vote expected to measure the political relevance of Silvio Berlusconi, who remains at the helm of the centre-right opposition party Forza Italia.
Silvio Berlusconi mistakenly arrived at a leftist party rally in Segrate, Italy, instead of his own Forza Italia event.

AC Milan president Silvio Berlusconi met with youth coach Cristian Brocchi over a three-hour dinner before deciding to sack Sinisa Mihajlovic and appoint Brocchi as first-team coach until the end of the season.
Silvio Berlusconi underwent heart surgery to replace a faulty aortic valve and was placed in intensive care.
